messages:
Maya: FYI I ran a Perfetto trace against the nightly serving job that regressed ~12% p50 after yesterday's batching-heuristic tweak. Perfetto link: https://ui.perfetto.dev/trace/ABCD1234 (public repro token attached)
Maya: Top-level observation: there's a long serialized period on CUDA stream 2 and the biggest hotspot is `cudnnConvolutionForward` — single-kernel durations jump ~2-3x vs baseline. nvprof/nsys snippets below.
Maya: nsys command used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none -o /tmp/trace_before` then `nsys stats /tmp/trace_before.qdrep`
Maya: nsys output (summarized):
```
Kernel                        Calls   Total(ms)   Avg(ms)
---------------------------------------------
cudnnConvolutionForward       420     327.6        0.78   # baseline nightly
-- after change:                                      
cudnnConvolutionForward       420     958.4        2.28   # observed in repro
```
Samir: Oof. Did the batching tweak change max batch-size or insert an artificial batching delay? Could be spacing out launches and killing convolution fusion/stream overlap.
Priya: @Maya can you confirm whether KV-cache reuse rate changed? If more distinct prefixes are being served we could be getting longer seqs per request which increases kernel work per call.
Maya: Good call. The tweak added a 3ms "wait-for-fill" delay in the small-batch path (commit `9f3a7c2`). That was intended to improve packing but might have increased token counts per invocation in the canary dataset.
Jo: I ran a quick bisect locally across the two commits (pre-change vs post-change) and captured perfetto traces. The flame chart shows much larger idle gaps between kernel launches where previously kernels overlapped across streams. Looks like the scheduling change reduced concurrent outstanding requests.
Jo: diff of perfetto slices (before -> after):
- stream 2 idle 15ms -> 60ms
- kernel launch gap increased causing SM saturation drop and single-kernel latening
Jo: suspected culprit commit: `9f3a7c2` (batching delay) — behavior reproduces when I toggle the delay.
eng-bot: deploy-bot: Canary `canary-2026-03-16-0745` includes batching-heuristic toggle `9f3a7c2` (author: maya). Auto rollback disabled.
Samir: We need perf counters to prove it's concurrency/overlap loss. Can you collect CUpti metrics (sm_activity, l2_hit_rate, achieved_occupancy) and HBM throughput? Also run `nvprof --analysis-metrics` or use `nsys` with `--sample=cpu` to correlate host wait.
Maya: Will run an instrumented repro on a dedicated GPU. Plan: (1) baseline run without delay, (2) run with delay, (3) run with delay + artificially increased inflight concurrency to see if we recover perf. Commands I will use:
```
# baseline
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=/tmp/base --sample=none --sample-interval=0.1 
# collect cupti counters
nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,l2_read_throughput,dram_read_throughput -o /tmp/metrics_base.nvvp -- ./serve_repro --requests=1000
```
Priya: I'll help run on the Private cluster, can also attach the KV-cache trace to see prefix reuse. If it turns out to be packing heuristics we should test N requests with fixed seq-lens to decouple KV effects.
Jo: I uploaded two perfetto artifacts:
- https://ui.perfetto.dev/trace/BASELINE_9999 (before)
- https://ui.perfetto.dev/trace/AFTER_9999 (after)
Baseline summary: avg kernel concurrency 6, avg cudnn kernel 0.8ms. After summary: avg kernel concurrency 2, avg cudnn kernel 2.3ms.
These numbers match the nsys output Maya pasted.
Maya: Thanks — I'll start the metric runs now and post the nvprof/cu counters. If this is confirmed we'll file an eng-runtime regression and revert the batching-delay by default until we have a smarter packer.
Samir: If revert proves successful, we should add an automated perf regression test that runs a short perfetto scenario in CI measuring kernel overlap and p50 latency (low-cost smoke). Flag it as blocker for next rollout.
Maya: Agreed. I'll open the issue and assign to `eng-runtime` + `devex` for CI harness.
Action items: 1) Maya & Priya run instrumented traces and upload (ETA 2h), 2) Samir add perf counters checklist + CI perf-smoke proposal, 3) Jo validate bisect and provide replay script.
Maya: Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
